impact:
`npm run test:all` exits 1 with ZERO test failures. The failure is `tests/oracle/mutation_check.py` reporting `SURVIVED  allowlist entry deleted while the gap remains`.

Not caused by T-009, and not a regression. The mutation deletes every `inventory.unexercised` entry whose shape is "blocks" and expects the checker to then complain "shape blocks declares --since". Commit 51e0a42 (ISS-029/ISS-024, parity coverage) closed all four unexercised gaps and set `"unexercised": []`. With an empty allowlist the mutation deletes nothing, the checker is unaffected, and it correctly reports SURVIVED.

The harness is behaving well here — it is saying, accurately, that this check is no longer exercised by anything. The bug is that a green `test:all` is now unreachable until the mutation is re-pointed.

This is the same defect class T-009 round 13 spent its whole time on: a check that passes for want of anything to act on. There it was a guard nothing reached; here it is a mutation whose target vanished when the gap it probed was legitimately fixed. Closing a coverage gap silently disarmed the mutation that proved the gap-tracking worked.

Two candidate fixes, and the choice is a real one:
- Re-point the mutation at a synthetic inventory that HAS an unexercised entry, so it tests the checker rather than the current data. This keeps the check alive permanently and decouples it from whether any real gap happens to exist.
- Or make an empty `unexercised` array skip this mutation explicitly and loudly, recording that it is inapplicable rather than surviving. Weaker, because "inapplicable" is one edit away from "never runs again".

The first is preferable: a mutation that only works while the codebase is imperfect is a mutation that retires exactly when the code gets good.

Reproduce: `npm run test:all; echo $?` -> 1, with no `not ok` lines anywhere in the output.
resolution:
RESOLVED — fixed in commit 60cf3d1 (2026-08-02), the same commit that filed this issue; the code fix landed but this record was never marked resolved. Re-verified on the current tree 2026-08-05: `python3 tests/oracle/mutation_check.py` exits 0 with "all 30 mutations caught", `npm run test:oracle` exits 0, and this issue's own reproduce command `npm run test:all; echo $?` now prints 0.

What landed is the first of the two candidate fixes this issue proposed (re-point rather than skip-loudly), in exactly the form recommended: the stale mutation no longer depends on the real inventory being imperfect.

1. The stale mutation ("allowlist entry deleted while the gap remains") was retired with an in-code tombstone at tests/oracle/mutation_check.py:73-77: "RETIRED ... ISS-029 exercised all four windowed args and emptied `unexercised`, so there is no entry to delete and the mutation became a no-op that always SURVIVED (ISS-059)." The tombstone also records where each of its two detection directions went.
2. Its declared-arg-without-observation direction is still observed by the existing "blocks shape gains an --until it never passes" mutation (mutation_check.py:57-59).
3. Its entry-hygiene direction moved to a NEW mutation, "allowlist entry names a shape no inventory declares" (mutation_check.py:78-81), which appends a synthetic bogus entry {shape: "bogus", arg: "--since"} — testing the checker rather than the current data, so it stays armed even with `unexercised: []` (inventory.json:212, still empty today).
4. The checker itself was hardened to make that new mutation catchable: tests/oracle/build.py:196-201 now fails on any `unexercised` entry naming a shape/arg no shape declares ("exempts nothing. Delete or fix the entry.") — previously such entries were read through `.get(..., set())` and silently tolerated.

Residual: none. No live ticket needed; the harness change is complete and green, and T-009 (whose closure check discovered this) closed in the same commit.

Fix commit: 60cf3d1 "Close ISS-059 and harden ISS-054; land T-009's closing ledger" — its message states "The mutation is retired with a tombstone ... and replaced: build.py now rejects allowlist entries naming shapes/args nothing declares ... 30/30 caught; test:all exits 0 again." Code: tests/oracle/mutation_check.py:73-77 tombstone ("RETIRED: 'allowlist entry deleted while the gap remains'. ISS-029 exercised all four windowed args and emptied `unexercised` ... (ISS-059)"); mutation_check.py:78-81 replacement mutation expecting "exempts nothing"; tests/oracle/build.py:196-201 new check ("`unexercised` entry {shape}/{arg} names a shape/arg no shape declares, so it exempts nothing. Severity medium was appropriate (harness-only defect, no product code wrong, but made green test:all unreachable); moot on closure.
title: test:all is red on a stale oracle mutation whose target no longer exists — the allowlist it probes was emptied by ISS-029
